title: PRAC concludes eye condition NAION is a very rare side effect of semaglutide medicines Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy
authors: European Medicines Agency, Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee
journal: European Medicines Agency news, 6 June 2025, revised 13 June 2025
result: After reviewing non-clinical studies, clinical trials, post-marketing surveillance and the literature, PRAC concluded that non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) is a very rare side effect of semaglutide, affecting up to 1 in 10,000 people taking it. Several large epidemiological studies suggest that semaglutide exposure in adults with type 2 diabetes is associated with an approximately two-fold increase in NAION risk against people not taking it, about one additional case per 10,000 person-years of treatment; clinical trial data also point to a slightly higher risk than placebo. Product information is to list NAION as very rare; patients with sudden loss of vision or rapidly worsening eyesight should contact their doctor, and semaglutide should be stopped if NAION is confirmed. The review was a post-authorisation measure resulting from a periodic safety update report assessment.
